behaviorChanges: Board gates fail closed: with backlogProvider/goalTracker enabled, provider-unavailable (gh missing, unauthenticated, or a token without the project read scope) now BLOCKS the pre-commit/pre-push board hook, guard-check's board-currency check, and methodology-status --strict/--fail-on-drift, printing the exact gh auth refresh remedy. Previously all three surfaces warned and passed, which silently disabled board enforcement on every machine with gh's default scopes -- the root cause behind recurring board-drift incidents. The new adapter key backlogProvider.unavailablePolicy ("block" default, "warn" as an explicit opt-down for deliberate offline work) is documented in the adapter schema; provider-disabled projects are unaffected.

requiredMigrations.command: gh auth refresh --hostname github.com -s read:project -s project
requiredMigrations.description: On every machine that runs provider-backed lanes: grant the gh token the GitHub Projects scopes the board gates need. Required wherever the adapter enables backlogProvider/goalTracker -- gh auth login's default scopes exclude read:project, and from 0.10.3 an unreadable authoritative board BLOCKS commits, pushes, and strict status instead of warning. Machines whose token already carries read:project and project need no action.

rollbackNotes: Pinning back to 0.10.2 restores warn-and-pass on provider-unavailable -- board enforcement silently stands down again on machines without the project scope. No on-disk state moves in either direction; the unavailablePolicy adapter key is simply ignored by older runtimes.
